caption: Cobb approved social media monitoring and more ALPRs in a 5-0 vote at the August 25 commission meeting. But why?
alt: Blue poster set in heavy orange and cream type: COBB APPROVES SOCIAL MEDIA MONITORING AND MORE ALPRS IN 5-0 VOTE, with a smaller line reading In 8. 25. BOC Meeting and a highlighted BUT WHY? beneath it. Orange starbursts sit in opposite corners, the deflock Cobb logo in the lower left, and an arrow points right along a chequered band at the foot.

caption: Flock says its cameras only read license plates. Then explain the one pointed at a community pool in Texas.
alt: Video still laid out as a phone screen on a blue grid background, headed Flock says their cameras only read license plates. If so, explain this. On the screen someone in a WHY? FLOCK CAMERAS t-shirt speaks to camera in front of a community swimming pool and houses, with a yellow arrow curving down towards the phone.

caption: The AJC reports Dunwoody residents were outraged to learn Flock used cameras from a children's gym to sell products to police departments.
alt: Video still over a repeating pattern of eyes and dollar bills. A panel reads Dunwoody residents outraged after discovering Flock used cameras from a child's gym to sell products to police departments. Below it a person in a grey jacket sits at a council dais, with the subtitle TO WATCH OUR KIDS underlined in orange.

caption: It doesn't have to be this way. We must stop the expansion of Flock Safety and predictive policing.
alt: Video still of a Flock camera on a black pole at the side of a suburban road, a car passing behind it. A panel at the top reads The impact of Flock cameras are a safety risk, a privacy risk, and are dangerous for communities as a whole, and the footage's subtitle reads every intersection.

caption: Thank you Cobb County! Yall showed up multiple times this week. The work doesn't stop. Our first Flock Town Hall is Thursday.
alt: Comic-styled collage headed THANK YOU: snapshots of residents protesting at a roadside with hand-made signs, a sign-making session, a DeFlock Q and A, and a speaker presenting to a seated audience, above the words For showing up.

caption: Happy National Week of Action! Two chances to get active today: Smyrna City Council at 7, and Flock 101 at 6:30 at South Cobb Library.
alt: Video still quoting a resident to Smyrna council: You've created a deep distrust between this council and Smyrna citizens, within a mile of my home alone 37 cameras are collecting my data. Below it, footage of the council chamber and a red banner reading Come speak out at City Council today located in City Hall at 7pm.

caption: Marietta keeps filling city council to capacity over the data center projects. The city seems more focused on policing our concerns than listening to them.
alt: Hand-drawn poster of two arms holding up a placard that reads WARNING! The city of Marietta is surveilling you!

caption: A portion of Marietta's Flock contract is expiring and we need you to call it out. Email the council, then sign up for public comment.
alt: Video title card reading AUGUST 12TH CITY COUNCIL MEETING in white and green type over a dark background of surveillance camera imagery.
